LPR (Landspatientregisteret) is a national register in Denmark that serves as a foundational data source for the [[adhd-databasen|ADHD-DATABASEN]] [^src1]. By extracting data directly from LPR, the system allows clinicians to avoid the administrative burden of double registration in a separate database [^src1]. However, this reliance on the national register carries a methodological risk: indicator results may be underestimated if performed procedures are missing or improperly registered in LPR [^src1].

The role of LPR is detailed in the 2024 annual ADHD database report, which outlines the data basis for evaluating ADHD treatment across Denmark [^src1]. This reporting cycle includes the introduction of quality indicator 11 for pharmacological treatment among adults, marking a significant expansion of the database's scope beyond children and adolescents [^src1]. Within this broader framework of systematic quality measurement and evidence-based practice, LPR operates alongside drug statistics to provide the necessary data for assessing regional and departmental performance, despite ongoing methodological challenges such as registration difficulties in the Capital Region and missing data from private hospitals [^src1].
